verdict.rationale: RustDesk's docs claim P2P end-to-end encryption and name the cryptographic basis (NaCl), but nothing in the pack documents the protocol itself (key exchange, relay handling, trust model), so the claim is largely asserted. A hands-on community report warns that encryption isn't enabled by default on a self-hosted setup. That limits the default posture rather than contradicting the capability. missing for 10: published protocol/key-exchange documentation, coverage of relay-path encryption, encryption-by-default on self-hosted servers, independent audit or corroboration.

support.subject: As an IT admin, sessions are encrypted end to end with the protocol documented, not just asserted

citations.quote: P2P connection with end-to-end encryption based on NaCl.
